what_happened.line: Voters passed Article 11, lengthening the demolition delay on historic houses, on a hand count; a motion to postpone it to the 2020 annual meeting was defeated.
Voters passed the plastic bag reduction bylaw, Article 17, by voice vote.
Voters authorized conveying a town parcel to a petitioner in Article 18, after an amendment to strike the petitioner's name failed on a hand count.
Voters passed over the noise control bylaw, Article 9, after long debate, with the motion taken ahead of a pending amendment.
Budget articles passed unanimously: line transfers, a special purpose stabilization deposit, first-year DPW union contract funding, a bond premium for paving and a sewer reserve transfer.

why_it_matters: Owners of older houses face a longer wait before a demolition can proceed, and shoppers and retailers will fall under a new plastic bag rule once the bylaw takes effect.
The union contract funding and stabilization deposit draw on the town budget, mostly taxes, while the bond premium reduces what the town must borrow for paving.
